pyqgis_plugin.name: RasterViz
pyqgis_plugin.description: RasterViz is a Matplotlib-style scientific raster visualization plugin for QGIS that enables publication-quality raster rendering directly within QGIS through an interactive interface without requiring an external Python environment.
pyqgis_plugin.about: RasterViz provides publication-quality raster visualization directly within QGIS without requiring an external Python environment. The plugin reproduces raster visualization aesthetics similar to rasterio.show() through an interactive Qt5-based interface. Key features include continuous single-band rendering with configurable colormap and contrast stretching options (percentile, min–max, and manual); discrete/classified raster visualization with automatic class detection, customizable colors, and label assignment; RGB composite rendering with independent band stretching; customizable pointed colorbars supporting adjustable geometry, orientation, and extend styles (both, max, min, or neither); coordinate tick formatting in DMS, DM, Decimal Degree, and native UTM/meter formats; real-time live preview supported by cached NumPy arrays for improved performance; and export functionality to PNG (300 DPI), SVG, TIFF, and PDF formats.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Map-X
pyqgis_plugin.description: Advanced spatial sync & compare tool with smart Z-ordering and real-time statistical legend (Lite Version).
pyqgis_plugin.about: Map-X (Lite Version) is a powerful spatial comparison tool tailored for Telecommunications, RF Engineering, and Network Optimization professionals. It transforms the standard QGIS interface into a dynamic command center, allowing users to compare datasets side-by-side without the hassle of toggling layers. Key features include: * Dual View Engine: Compare two maps side-by-side with draggable splitters. (Triple and Quad views are available in the Pro version). * Bi-Directional Live Sync: Panning and zooming in one map instantly synchronizes across the active canvas, ensuring you never lose spatial context. * Intelligent Statistical Legend: An auto-generating, compact legend that calculates real-time data distribution (Sample Count & Percentage) based strictly on the active canvas extent and priority layers. * Smart Layering (Z-Order): Automatically forces critical physical infrastructure data (Sites, Gcells) to the top layer, ensuring they are never obscured by drive test data or coverage polygons. * Ultra-Minimalist UI: Designed to maximize map visibility. (Layout Export and Crosshair Tracking features are available in the Pro version). Upgrade to the Pro Version via Gumroad or Lynk.id to unlock up to 4 synchronized views, crosshair tracking, and layout exporting!

pyqgis_plugin.name: Districts Modeler
pyqgis_plugin.description: GIS-based district energy modeler for preparing, managing and visualising data for dynamic simulation in IDA Districts.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Districts Modeler is a free QGIS plugin developed by EQUA for creating, managing and preparing map-based models of district energy systems for simulation with IDA Districts, EQUA’s district energy simulation software. Districts Modeler and IDA Districts are products of EQUA. The plugin is free to use; detailed dynamic simulation is carried out in IDA Districts.
The Districts Modeler helps users build digital representations of district heating, district cooling and low-temperature energy networks by combining buildings, pipes, substations, energy plants, storage systems and consumers in one GIS-based environment. The plugin makes it easier to understand how a thermal energy network is structured, how different components are connected and how system data can be prepared for further analysis. Districts Modeler supports the preparation of consistent, simulation-ready models by providing tools for spatial data processing, network topology generation, data management, validation and visualisation directly in QGIS. Model data is stored in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database and can be exchanged with IDA Districts for detailed dynamic simulation.
Districts Modeler supports the preparation of consistent, simulation-ready models by providing tools for spatial data processing, network topology generation, data management, validation and visualisation directly in QGIS. Model data is stored in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database and can be exchanged with IDA Districts for detailed dynamic simulation.
The physical simulation itself is performed in IDA Districts, where users can analyse thermal and hydraulic network behaviour, building energy demand, energy sources, storage systems, control strategies and system performance over time.
Typical applications include district heating and cooling planning, network modelling, transformation studies, analysis of existing infrastructure, preparation of low-temperature or bidirectional network concepts, integration of renewable energy sources and support for research and planning projects.
Districts Modeler is intended for engineers, utilities, planners, municipalities, researchers and other stakeholders who want to prepare transparent and simulation-ready district energy models for use with IDA Districts.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Fill Attribute Gaps
pyqgis_plugin.description: Interpolate missing (NULL) attribute values between known key points using linear, nearest-neighbor, cubic spline, or step interpolation.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Fill NULL gaps in any numeric attribute field. Pick your layer, choose a sort column and a target column with some values filled in and some NULL, select an interpolation method, and the plugin fills in the blanks. Existing values (including 0) are never overwritten. Supports full undo with Ctrl+Z.
Methods: - Linear: straight-line interpolation between key points (default) - Nearest neighbor: copy the closest known value - Cubic spline: smooth curve through key points (needs scipy and 3+ keys) - Step (forward fill): carry last known value forward
Common use cases: filling elevation profiles, chainage/milepost values, sensor readings, survey data completion, utility network attributes.

pyqgis_plugin.name: AtQuery
pyqgis_plugin.description: AI Chat for QGIS
pyqgis_plugin.about:
AtQuery: Local GeoAI Assistant for QGIS
AtQuery is a QGIS plugin that allows users to perform GIS queries, data inspection, and geospatial workflows using natural language. Instead of manually navigating menus or writing PyQGIS scripts, users can interact with QGIS through conversational commands.
The plugin uses a toolbox-routing architecture to identify the most relevant GIS skill domain before passing the request to a local language model running through Ollama. By loading only the required GIS tools into context, AtQuery improves tool-selection reliability and responsiveness on lightweight local models.
Features: • Natural language GIS queries and workflow automation • Data inspection, selection, vector processing, raster analysis, and export tools • Toolbox-based routing for efficient tool selection • Fully local execution through Ollama (no cloud APIs required) • Transparent tool execution and result display • Extensible community toolbox for additional capabilities
Designed for GIS professionals, researchers, and students, including those with limited GIS experience, who want to explore and perform geospatial workflows through natural language within QGIS.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Fishnet Creator
pyqgis_plugin.description: Create fishnet polygon/polyline grids equivalent to ArcGIS Create Fishnet. Pixel-perfect raster alignment, unit selector, rotation support, clip to boundary, label points, and temporary layer support.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Fishnet Creator replicates the ArcGIS "Create Fishnet" workflow directly inside QGIS.
HOW TO USE: 1. Set your output path (or leave blank for a temporary scratch layer) 2. Define the grid extent — use a layer, canvas, or type coordinates manually 3. Set Origin and Y-Axis coordinates (Y-Axis controls rotation angle) 4. Enter Cell Width and Height, or Rows and Columns (auto-syncs Opposite Corner) 5. Choose CRS, geometry type, and optionally create label points 6. Click OK — the fishnet is generated and loaded into your map
KEY FEATURES: - Exact ArcGIS Create Fishnet UI layout (Origin, Y-Axis, Cell Size, Rows/Cols, Opposite Corner) - Grid rotation via Y-Axis coordinate - Pixel-perfect raster alignment using GDAL geotransform - Cell size unit selector: metres, km, feet, miles, yards, nautical miles, degrees - Live coverage feedback showing total rows × columns - Clip output to any polygon layer boundary - Optional centroid label points layer - Polygon or Polyline geometry output - Temporary scratch layer mode (no file required) - Compatible with QGIS 3.x and 4.x
REQUIREMENTS: - QGIS 3.0 or higher (including QGIS 4.x) - No extra Python libraries required

pyqgis_plugin.name: LiDAR Relief Visualization
pyqgis_plugin.description: A free, open-source QGIS toolkit with 31 Processing algorithms for archaeological LiDAR visualization and terrain analysis. Reveal subtle earthworks, prepare point clouds, compare surveys, combine LiDAR with satellite imagery, validate anomalies in the field, and produce reproducible research outputs.
pyqgis_plugin.about: LiDAR Relief Visualization is a free and open-source archaeological terrain-analysis toolkit for QGIS and part of the Dig:Tools ecosystem. Its 31 Processing algorithms help archaeologists, heritage professionals, and landscape researchers examine digital elevation models and LiDAR point clouds for subtle features such as ditches, banks, mounds, hollow ways, scarps, platforms, quarrying, and disturbed ground. Core tools include multi-directional hillshade, SLRM, Sky-View Factor, anisotropic Sky-View Factor, positive and negative openness, Local Dominance, MSTP, e4MSTP, Terrain Ruggedness Index, slope, VAT, Simple Red Relief, PCA composites, visualization blending, and batch processing with landscape presets. Extended workflows support LAS/LAZ ground filtering, PDAL processing, multi-temporal DEM comparison, LiDAR and Sentinel-2 fusion, Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF export, interactive web maps, QField survey packages, reproducible visualization recipes, PDF reporting, and optional ONNX-based feature detection. Core terrain tools work with libraries supplied by QGIS. Specialized capabilities use clearly identified optional packages and remain isolated, so missing optional dependencies do not prevent the plugin from loading. The plugin supports QGIS 3 and QGIS 4 and is tested through automated numerical, packaging, clean-runtime, and desktop-loader checks. It supports transparent, reproducible research without subscription fees or proprietary lock-in. Visualizations and automated detections are interpretive aids rather than archaeological classifications. Assess potential features using complementary evidence and, where appropriate, field validation. New to the plugin? Run "Visualisation Contact Sheet" to compare techniques on your own DEM in seconds, then open any algorithm and press Help for the full user guide. The guide also ships inside the plugin folder as USER_GUIDE.md, and is online at https://github.com/dig-tools/lidar-relief-qgis-plugin/blob/main/lidar_relief/USER_GUIDE.md

pyqgis_plugin.name: CityStockID Automated Urban Diagnostic AUD
pyqgis_plugin.description:
CityStockID Automated Urban Diagnostic AUD is a QGIS plugin designed to generate automated urban diagnostics from temporally harmonized gridded building stock data for Indonesia.
The plugin analyzes WorldPop and Google Open Buildings temporal building stock data at 100 m resolution to identify building growth, footprint expansion, vertical or mass densification, compact intensification, urban shrinking indication, morphological pressure, urban fringe dynamics, and preliminary spatial planning policy directions.
CityStockID supports evidence based urban and regional planning by transforming multi year building stock rasters into interpretable spatial indicators, zonal diagnostics, visual analytics, and automated HTML reporting.
The tool supports a wide range of planning applications including: 1. Urban growth and expansion monitoring 2. Building intensity and morphological pressure assessment 3. KDB, KLB, and KDH proxy screening 4. Urban shrinking indication and regeneration diagnostics 5. Compact growth and densification evaluation 6. Urban fringe and sprawl risk monitoring 7. RDTR and spatial planning policy support 8. Infrastructure capacity pressure screening 9. Strategic urban diagnostic reporting
pyqgis_plugin.about:
CityStockID provides an integrated automated urban diagnostic framework for analyzing Indonesia specific building stock dynamics using temporally harmonized gridded raster data.
The plugin combines remote sensing based building stock information, raster change analysis, zonal statistics, spatial morphology indicators, urban intensity proxies, and rule based planning diagnostics to support urban and regional planning decisions.
It generates key diagnostic indicators such as building stock change, percent growth, CAGR, KDB proxy, KLB proxy, KDH pressure, vertical intensity, average footprint size, perimeter surface ratio, compactness proxy, sprawl risk index, densification score, morphological pressure index, and urban intensity index.
CityStockID also classifies zonal urban dynamics into categories such as Urban Shrinking Indication, Growth Hotspot, Compact Intensification, Footprint Expansion, Vertical or Mass Densification, Moderate Growth, Stable or Low Change, Decline or Noise Candidate, and No Data.
The plugin produces preliminary policy directions through a 9 class classifier including Urban Shrinking Regeneration Direction, Sprawl Control, FAR Audit and Vertical Transition, Green or Open Space Priority and Overbuilt Control, Intensity and Infrastructure Capacity Audit, Anticipate Intensification and Guide Compact Growth, Footprint Expansion Monitoring, Stable or Low Change Area, and General Monitoring.
Outputs include a spatial diagnostic layer, raster summaries, zonal summary tables, optional XLSX workbook, modern PNG visualizations, and an automated HTML diagnostic report with planning conclusions.
CityStockID is designed for research, planning practice, spatial monitoring, RDTR support, urban growth assessment, and evidence based policy diagnostics in Indonesian urban and regional planning contexts.

pyqgis_plugin.name: SoilTool
pyqgis_plugin.description: Interactive soil profile visualization tool for QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Scientific tool for visualising and managing soil profiles directly in QGIS vector layers. It allows adding horizons with custom properties like texture, color, and boundaries. No external Python libraries required.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Numerar Ruta
pyqgis_plugin.description: Sequentially numbers points along a route line based on spatial order.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Tool that opens a modal dialog to sequentially number points that fall on a route line, in the order defined by the line's geometry from start to end. Points at the same location share the same number, and junction points between consecutive route segments preserve their existing number to avoid gaps when chaining tramos. Useful for utility inventories (poles, luminaires, valves, manholes) where the numbering must follow the physical route rather than the feature ID order. Requirements: the points layer and the line layer must share a CRS suitable for distance calculation (geographic or projected). No external Python dependencies. Differences from similar tools: unlike attribute-based sorting or fid-based numbering, this plugin uses lineLocatePoint to project each point onto the line and sort by along-line distance, which correctly handles curved routes and points added out of capture order.

pyqgis_plugin.about: Saves the current QGIS project automatically every 20 minutes, whenever a new layer is added, and whenever layer symbology changes. Works globally for any project without per-project configuration.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GCN-HSI
pyqgis_plugin.description: Semi-automated Great Crested Newt Habitat Suitability Index (HSI) calculator. Created from improvements made to Oldham's (2000) original scoring system.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Calculates the Great Crested Newt (GCN) Habitat Suitability Index for up to 10 candidate ponds per run. Now contains two tools. Remote Assessment tool automates SI1 - SI6 scoring (designed for fast pre-screening only). Full assessment requires field survey data. Supports per pond override to automated variables if field data is available. Includes road barrier detection to exclude habitats and ponds on far side of a road. Output is a polygon layer with per pond HSI scoring and traffic light symbology. Hope it helps.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QWorkspaceSwitcher
pyqgis_plugin.description: Create, manage and apply named QGIS interface configurations (workspaces). Switch between different working environments in one click from the toolbar.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
QWorkspace Switcher allows QGIS users to create, save and apply named interface configurations called workspaces. Each workspace defines which panels (QDockWidget), toolbars (QToolBar) and menus are visible, and how they are organized in the QGIS main window.
Key features: - Create workspaces by capturing the current QGIS interface - Apply a workspace in one click from the toolbar - Configure button style (text, icon, icon+text, text+icon) - Assign a custom icon to each workspace - Add dropdown menus from other plugins per workspace - Show or hide the QGIS menu bar per workspace - Declarative .psp.json system for third-party plugins - Blacklist system for deleted plugin workspaces - Export/import workspace configuration file - Emergency shortcut Ctrl+Shift+M to restore menu bar
Originally developed at CNR (Compagnie Nationale du Rhône) for hydraulic modeling workflows. Designed as a generic, domain-independent tool for any QGIS user or organization.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Adnan Benaboud — Compagnie Nationale du Rhône (CNR)

Outputs include Iron Oxide, Ferrous Minerals, Clay Minerals, Alunite, Kaolinite, Carbonate, Gossan, Silica, and vegetation indices - each saved as an individual GeoTIFF.

pyqgis_plugin.name: EquiMap Spatial Inequality Intelligence
pyqgis_plugin.description: EquiMap Spatial Inequality Intelligence is a QGIS plugin designed to generate spatial inequality diagnostics from two numeric polygon variables through bivariate mapping, inequality metrics, spatial autocorrelation analysis, and modern visual reporting.
pyqgis_plugin.about: EquiMap provides an integrated spatial inequality intelligence framework for QGIS. It combines bivariate choropleth mapping, Gini Index, Theil T Index, Hoover Index, Lorenz curve, concentration curve, Pearson and Spearman correlation, Global Moran I, Local Moran or LISA, Bivariate Moran, and Bivariate Local Moran or BiLISA. The recommended logic is directional: Variable Y represents demand, need, pressure, risk, exposure, or vulnerability, while Variable X represents service, supply, access, infrastructure, capacity, support, or resilience. Outputs include a classified spatial layer, QML style file, bivariate poster map, legend PNG, Lorenz curve PNG, concentration curve PNG, Moran scatterplot PNG, Bivariate Moran scatterplot PNG, LISA map PNG, BiLISA map PNG, summary dashboard PNG, summary CSV, priority ranking CSV, and automated HTML spatial inequality report.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoLogic Flight Planner
pyqgis_plugin.description: Generates high-efficiency flight routes with terrain following, compatible with the UAV.COM API (DJI Fly).
pyqgis_plugin.about: The GeoLogic Flight Planner is a professional-grade QGIS plugin designed for efficient drone mapping and aerial photogrammetry. It integrates spatial analysis with drone kinematics to generate high-efficiency flight paths that automatically adapt to terrain via Digital Elevation Models (DEMs). The plugin bridges the gap between GIS and field operations by translating complex mapping logic into native DJI WPML-compliant KMZ missions. Key features include intelligent waypoint densification to safeguard controller memory, kinematic-based flight time estimation for enhanced safety, and advanced route optimization that minimizes battery consumption and flight time. Built to provide an autonomous, transparent, and robust alternative to proprietary software, it empowers field professionals to plan and execute precise missions directly from their GIS workspace.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Water Masking Plugin
pyqgis_plugin.description: A comprehensive tool for extracting water masks and generating smoothed waterbody polygons from multispectral satellite imagery.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Water Masking Plugin is a specialized QGIS toolkit designed to extract accurate water masks and generate smoothed waterbody polygons from multispectral satellite imagery.
Core Workflow: 1-Indices Calculation: Calculates NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), MNDWI (Modified Normalized Difference Water Index), and NWI (New Water Index). 2-Water Masking Equation: Uses the equation (MNDWI > 0) AND (NWI > 0) AND (NDVI < 0.1) to extract the water mask. 3-Noise Removal: Applies a sieve filter to remove isolated noise pixels. 4-Geometry Smoothing: Rounds the sharp stair-step edges of the final polygon.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Rosa dos Ventos Geomagnética (Magnetic Declination)
pyqgis_plugin.description: Generates an interactive compass rose demonstrating the magnetic declination of the day based on the WMM-2025 model. Exports to SVG/PNG and adds it as a vector layer.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Plugin created by Alessandro Pimentel - Phone: +55 (91) 98505-6742. This plugin calculates the magnetic declination of any location on the globe for the current date using the World Magnetic Model (WMM-2025). It displays a stylized and professional compass rose in real-time, allowing export to SVG/PNG and insertion of the geometry as a layer in the map.

pyqgis_plugin.description: Advanced schema-union vector layer converter, name-collision protector, and database compiler tool.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Building ACR
pyqgis_plugin.description: A QGIS-based plugin for calculating building- and climate-specific hourly Air Change Rates (ACR) at urban scale, integrating wind speed correction and the 3ZLPM model for improved infiltration modelling in UBEM applications.
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin computes hourly building- and climate-specific Air Change Rates (ACR) to improve infiltration modelling in Urban Building Energy Modelling (UBEM). It integrates wind speed corrections at facade level using urban canyon algorithms, outdoor temperature correction via the Urban Weather Generator (UWG/UMEP), and hourly ACR simulation using a Three-Zone Lumped Parameter Model (3ZLPM) or CONTAM. Inputs include building geometry, air permeability, roughness length, and hourly weather data.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Yasemin Usta; Xuan Zhou; Guglielmina Mutani

pyqgis_plugin.about: Universal XY Converter is a powerful QGIS plugin for coordinate conversion between any Coordinate Reference Systems (CRS) available in QGIS, with native support for BFTM (Burkina Faso Transverse Mercator). Features: single conversion, batch CSV processing, interactive map picking, support for DD, DMS (with French notations O for Ouest, E for Est, N for Nord, S for Sud), and meters format. Now supports Clarke 1880 and Adindan in degrees and UTM zones (all zones 1-60 N/S) with region-specific parameters: West Africa (-118,-14,218) and Cameroon (-166,-15,204). Multilingual support: French/English automatically based on QGIS language.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Otomatisasi D3TLH
pyqgis_plugin.description: Automated D3TLH analysis and environmental carrying capacity assessment tools for QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Otomatisasi D3TLH is a QGIS plugin developed to streamline and automate workflows for D3TLH (Environmental Carrying Capacity and Environmental Carrying Capability) assessments. The plugin integrates demographic, ecological, environmental, and spatial analysis models into a unified processing framework, reducing manual data preparation and calculation efforts. It provides tools for generating standardized outputs that support environmental planning, regional development assessment, and decision-making processes. The plugin was developed by the Directorate of Environmental Impact Prevention and Regional Sectoral Policy, Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Indonesia (KLH/BPLH), with support from Yayasan Lokus Bijak Hijau Lestari (LOKAHITA).
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Fadillah Azhar Deaudin Kurniawan, Sitarani Safitri, Dini Aprilia Norvyani, Suchi Rahmadani, Fariz Rizaldy Wibowo

pyqgis_plugin.description: Sistema de Inteligencia Territorial y Auditoría Catastral para la deconstrucción, validación masiva del NPN (22/30 dígitos) e integración en tiempo real con la Ventanilla Única de Registro (VUR).
pyqgis_plugin.about: NPN Decoder es la solución empresarial definitiva para ingenieros catastrales, tasadores, desarrolladores inmobiliarios y gestores de infraestructura en Colombia. Este plugin automatiza la validación de calidad y deconstrucción analítica del Número Predial Nacional (NPN 22 y 30 dígitos) bajo estándares LADM-COL. Integra un potente motor de consulta bidireccional en tiempo real con la Ventanilla Única de Registro (VUR-SNR) para confrontar áreas elipsoidales calculadas en QGIS contra áreas jurídicas registradas en los folios de matrícula, alertando al instante sobre embargos, gravámenes y discrepancias espaciales críticas. Diseñado para optimizar los procesos de debida diligencia de tierras, control de calidad de bases de datos vectoriales catastrales y saneamiento predial con precisión analítica excepcional.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Topology Checker Pro
pyqgis_plugin.description: Detect, visualise & fix vector topology errors — with canvas markers, zoom-to-error, and step-by-step fix guidance
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Topology Checker Pro scans any vector layer for geometry errors (null geometry, invalid geometry, self-intersections, duplicates, overlaps, gaps, dangles, multipart features) and displays the results in a clean docked panel.
Key features: • Colour-coded markers drawn directly on the map canvas for every error • Click any error row to zoom to it and see a bright yellow highlight • Full-feature orange outline shows exactly which polygon/line is affected • Solution panel: plain-English explanation + numbered manual fix steps • One-click Auto-Fix for Invalid Geometry, Self-Intersections and Multipart • Prev / Next navigation through all errors • Export results to CSV • Works with QGIS 3.x (Qt5/PyQt5) and QGIS 4.x (Qt6/PyQt6)

pyqgis_plugin.name: Raster Clipper
pyqgis_plugin.description: Clip raster layers by vector mask with All-Touched boundary control and detailed pixel statistics.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Raster Clipper lets you clip any raster layer using a vector boundary (SHP, GPKG, or any loaded vector layer) with fine-grained pixel-inclusion control.
Key features: • All Touched mode — include every pixel that even touches the boundary, not just pixels whose centre falls inside (uses GDAL CUTLINE_ALL_TOUCHED). • Temporary file support — clip directly to an auto-generated temp path; no need to choose an output file for quick exploratory work. • Detailed pixel statistics — WIDTH_IN_PIXELS, HEIGHT_IN_PIXELS, TOTAL_PIXEL_COUNT, NODATA_PIXEL_COUNT, and VALID_PIXEL_COUNT per band, displayed in a styled dark terminal panel after every clip. • Auto-loads the clipped result into the QGIS canvas. • GeoPackage-aware — correctly resolves |layername= source paths. • Robust nodata detection — handles float NaN, integer overflow, and cases where GDAL does not write nodata metadata to the output file.
Built with pure GDAL (gdal.WarpOptions) for maximum compatibility.

pyqgis_plugin.name: CityLume Planner NTL Based Urban Structure and Planning Intelligence
pyqgis_plugin.description:
CityLume Planner is a QGIS plugin for analyzing nighttime light dynamics, urban structure, planning mismatch, future urban centers, and spatial planning action priorities using NTL time series, POI, building, road, population, and spatial plan allocation data.
The plugin transforms multi year NTL and supporting spatial datasets into urban dynamics classes, future core probability, shrinking risk, center hierarchy, planning mismatch typologies, and action matrix recommendations for evidence based urban and regional planning.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
CityLume Planner provides an integrated spatial planning intelligence framework for diagnosing urban growth, decline, center hierarchy, and planning mismatch using nighttime light time series and complementary urban datasets.
It combines NTL trend analysis, POI and building aggregation, road accessibility, optional population raster, optional spatial plan allocation, and optional planned center data to produce interpretable planning indicators and recommendations.
Outputs include an analysis grid, future core candidates, CSV and XLSX summaries, modern PNG maps and charts, GIF animations, metadata JSON, and an automatic diagnostic TXT report.
CityLume Planner is designed for urban structure evaluation, spatial plan monitoring, future service center detection, growth control analysis, urban regeneration diagnostics, and evidence based planning policy support.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GEE GPR Phenology
pyqgis_plugin.description: A QGIS plugin for Sentinel-2 biophysical variable retrieval, temporal gap filling, and land surface phenology analysis using Gaussian Process Regression.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GEE GPR Phenology implements a complete workflow for Sentinel-2 BOA/L2A imagery, including spectral GPR prediction, temporal gap filling with an RBF kernel, double logistic fitting, and land surface phenology metrics such as SOS, EOS, POS and LOS. Since version 1.5.0, the plugin includes automatic layer loading with QGIS symbology and groups, PDF/CSV reports, heterogeneous raster grid correction for LSP processing, duplicate-date handling, and multilingual support in Spanish, English and Portuguese. Version 1.5.18 resolves the Qt6 compatibility findings reported by the QGIS Plugin Repository by using scoped QGIS enum members with QGIS 3 fallbacks and a Qt5/Qt6-compatible dialog execution method. Version 1.5.17 removed subprocess-based dependency installation, replaced silent exception handling with explicit debug logging, and retained manual dependency instructions. The official contact email remains jfloresr@unal.edu.co. All mathematical, modelling, GPR, gap-filling, phenology, Sentinel-2 index, model data, and Processing algorithm logic remains unchanged. Note for QGIS 4.0.x / Python 3.12: in some installations, functional libraries such as rasterio may not be available in the QGIS Python environment by default. If rasterio is missing, GEE download may work but raster harmonization, gap filling, GPR raster prediction, or LSP processing can stop with ModuleNotFoundError. Use the plugin Info tab to view manual dependency instructions, or install rasterio in the QGIS Python environment before running those workflows. For security, the plugin never executes pip, ensurepip, shell commands, or other external processes. QGIS 3.x testing remains the recommended production path until all required Python wheels are confirmed in the target QGIS 4 environment. This release does not change the mathematical or modelling logic.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Adapted for QGIS by Jesus Enrique Flores Riera

pyqgis_plugin.name: THERMATO (Thermal Risk Mapping and Analysis Tool)
pyqgis_plugin.description: This plugin analyzes the correlation between heat exposure risk, land surface characteristics, and socio-economic vulnerability, and provides automated spatial estimation of urban heat risk patterns.
pyqgis_plugin.about: THERMATO integrates land surface temperature (LST), vegetation cover (NDVI), built-up intensity (NDBI), and demographic indicators to model urban heat risk automatically. This plugin provides classified heat risk maps and zonal statistics, enabling rapid assessment of hazard, socio-economic vulnerability, and adaptive capacity. By linking satellite-derived thermal conditions with population distribution and land cover change, THERMATO reveals how urban expansion and reduced vegetation intensify local heat exposure. Designed for climate risk analysts and urban planning agencies, it supports evidence-based decision making and prioritization of high-risk thermal zones.

pyqgis_plugin.name: URGREECS Urban Green Equity Analytics 3-30-300
pyqgis_plugin.description:
URGREECS Urban Green Equity Analytics 3-30-300 is a QGIS plugin for evaluating urban green performance, public green space access, and spatial equity using the integrated 3-30-300 framework.
The plugin combines building level tree proximity analysis, block level canopy adequacy, 300 meter public green space access, population service assessment, vulnerable population exposure, and optional kelurahan or administrative aggregation.
URGREECS transforms canopy height models, population rasters, vulnerable group rasters, building footprints, urban blocks, public green space layers, and administrative boundaries into interpretable green equity indicators, priority classes, maps, charts, CSV summaries, and planning recommendations.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
URGREECS Urban Green Equity Analytics 3-30-300 provides an integrated spatial analytics framework for diagnosing the distribution, accessibility, and equity of urban greenery.
The plugin operationalizes the 3-30-300 urban green concept by measuring whether buildings have sufficient nearby tree canopy, whether urban blocks reach at least 30 percent green cover, and whether residents are within 300 meters of public green space.
URGREECS extends conventional green access analysis into green equity analytics by incorporating total population and optional vulnerable population groups such as babies or young children, women, and elderly residents.
The plugin produces building indicators, block indicators, administrative summaries, green equity scores, priority classes, CSV outputs, and modern PNG insights including dashboards, charts, and map based visualizations.
URGREECS is designed for urban green infrastructure planning, spatial justice assessment, environmental justice analysis, urban health diagnostics, RTH planning, climate responsive urban planning, kelurahan level prioritization, and evidence based policy support.

pyqgis_plugin.name: PanoramaView360

pyqgis_plugin.about: PanoramaView360 allows you to click on features in a vector layer and instantly open the associated 360-degree panoramic image in your browser using an A-Frame based viewer. It supports two path modes: (1) full path stored in an attribute field, or (2) filename stored in a field with a separately specified image folder (with optional subfolder search). Features include map highlight on selection, a local HTTP server for image serving, and mouse-wheel zoom in the panorama viewer.PanoramaView360は、ベクタレイヤ上のフィーチャをクリックすると、対応する360度パノラマ画像をA-Frameベースのビューアでブラウザ上に即座に表示できるプラグインです。画像パスは、属性フィールドに格納されたフルパスまたはファイル名のいずれかで指定でき、画像フォルダを別途指定することで柔軟に参照できます（サブフォルダ検索にも対応）。また、選択した地点のハイライト表示、ローカルHTTPサーバによる画像配信、パノラマビューアでのマウスホイールズームなどの機能を備えています。

pyqgis_plugin.name: Ugsurv

pyqgis_plugin.name: GISNET QTools

GISNET QTools to wtyczka zaprojektowana w celu ułatwienia pozyskiwania danych z polskich portali rządowych.
Jej celem jest umożliwienie użytkownikom szybkiego wyszukiwania interesujących ich danych i przekierowania ich do odpowiedniego portalu zewnętrznego poprzez kliknięcie na mapie.
Wtyczka wykorzystuje portal OBLIVIEW firmy MGGP Aero Sp. z o.o. (https://obliview.com).
To wstępna wersja wtyczki, która będzie rozszerzana o dodatkowe funkcje.
Wtyczka wykorzystuje ikony wygenerowane przez Flaticon.com

Its goal is to enable users to quickly search for data of interest and redirect them to the appropriate external portal by clicking on the map.
The plugin utilizes the OBLIVIEW portal from MGGP Aero Sp. z o.o. (https://obliview.com).

The plugin uses icons generated by Flaticon.com

pyqgis_plugin.name: MJ-Chainage

Users can select any point layer and line layer from the current QGIS project. The plugin automatically creates a chainage field if it does not exist and calculates chainage based on the nearest line geometry. Suitable for roads, rivers, canals, drainage networks, pipelines, survey, irrigation, and infrastructure projects. Developed by MJNETWORK.You can support development via donation using PhonePe: <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mmjayswal/QG_Code/main/GIS_Donation.JPG"><b>Click here to View UPI QR Code</b></a>

pyqgis_plugin.name: MJ Chainage Draw
pyqgis_plugin.description: Draw continuous polylines with exact chainage inputs and optional click-to-distance auto calculation.
pyqgis_plugin.about: MJ Chainage Draw is an advanced QGIS map tool designed for surveying, highway engineering, and pipeline mapping. It allows users to interactively create a continuous polyline by either entering specific segment lengths manually or using the map click distance automatically (by pressing Enter). The tool perfectly handles coordinate transformations (Canvas to Layer CRS) to eliminate ellipsoidal distance calculation mismatches, tracks real-time rubber band previews, supports standard snapping, and includes seamless multi-step Ctrl+Z undo operations. It automatically auto-creates and populates LENGTH and CHAINAGE attributes (e.g., 1+250 format) on a single continuous feature path. Developed by MJNETWORK. Support development through the Homepage QR Code.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Advanced Layout Manager Browser

pyqgis_plugin.about: Layout Manager Browser is a QGIS productivity plugin designed to improve the management of print layouts in projects containing large numbers of figures, plans and report outputs. The plugin introduces custom groups and subgroups, search tools, favourites, colour-coded categories and batch export capabilities. Group information is stored safely within the QGIS project file, allowing project organisation to be shared between users while keeping layouts as standard QGIS layouts. Compatible with QGIS 3.x, QGIS 4.x, Qt5 and Qt6.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Pipeline Engineer
pyqgis_plugin.description: A pipe network modelling and BOM generation tool for compressible and incompressible flow.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Abstracts hydraulic models and material lists directly from map layers. Offers tools for validating network topography.

pyqgis_plugin.name: PCA Band Selector
pyqgis_plugin.description: Analyze multiband raster using PCA to find the most unique and informative band combinations
pyqgis_plugin.about:
PCA Band Selector performs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on any multiband raster (Landsat, Sentinel, AVIRIS, etc.) to identify which bands carry the most unique spectral information. It recommends optimal 2, 3, and 4-band combinations for classification and visualization by maximizing information content and minimizing inter-band redundancy.
Features: - Explained variance chart per Principal Component - PC Loadings matrix (color coded) - Band uniqueness scores ranked - Best 2/3/4-band combination recommendations - Inter-band correlation matrix - Auto memory management for large images - Export results as TXT report or CSV - Compatible with QGIS 3.x and QGIS 4.x (Qt5 and Qt6)

pyqgis_plugin.name: MultiViewManager

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS Time Tracker

It provides live monitoring through a floating timer widget, detailed dashboard analytics, and report exports in CSV, Excel, and PDF formats. Daily, weekly, and monthly working-time summaries help GIS professionals, freelancers, researchers, and organizations analyze project effort and productivity.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Feature Navigation Dock

pyqgis_plugin.name: ImageQualityToolset
pyqgis_plugin.description: Computes MTF and SNR image quality metrics from satellite imagery using Knife Edge, Bridge (Pulse), and Variogram methods.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
The Image Quality Toolset is a QGIS plugin developed in the context of the ESA AI4QC project. It targets remote sensing Calibration/Validation users as a supporting tool for Quality Control (QC) of satellite imagery.
It integrates into the QGIS Processing Toolbox and provides a command-line interface to perform image quality assessments from Regions of Interest (ROIs) defined on an input raster. ROIs are processed to derive Modulation Transfer Function (MTF) and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) image quality measures. Results are exported as diagnostic PNG figures and cumulative GeoPackage reports.
Three methods are available: - MTF Knife Edge Method: estimates MTF from a sharp contrast transition between two uniform areas. Derived metrics include MTF@Nyquist, MTF30, MTF50, FWHM, RER, HEE, and R². - MTF Bridge (Pulse) Method: estimates MTF from a narrow pulse target (bridge structure). - SNR Variogram Method: computes SNR by combining a Histogram method and a Variogram method, with per-pixel local SNR estimation.
Each method requires an input raster and a polygon ROI (shapefile). Radiometric scale and offset parameters allow conversion from raw DN to radiance. Results are accumulated across runs in a GeoPackage report, one feature per analysis, with full metadata and geometry.
The plugin uses a dual-license model: the QGIS integration layer is released under GPL v3; the core signal-processing algorithms (MTF, SNR, ESF models, variogram) are released under Apache 2.0.

pyqgis_plugin.about: A plugin designed to get biodiversity data from a number of Living Atlases into QGIS. These include GBIF, the Atlas of Living Australia, Austria, Brazil, Flanders, Kew Gardens, Spain, Sweden, and the United Kingdom.

pyqgis_plugin.name: PANSA DroneMap Downloader
pyqgis_plugin.description: Pobieranie i filtrowanie struktur przestrzeni powietrznej oraz stref geograficznych BSP bezpośrednio z serwerów PAŻP (DroneMap). / Downloading and filtering airspace structures and UAS geographical zones directly from PANSA (DroneMap) servers.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
[PL] Wtyczka pozawala na bezpośrednie pobieranie z oficjalnego interfejsu serwerowego PAŻP (api.dronemap.pansa.pl) pliku KML, obrazującego strefy przestrzeni powietrznej i strefy geograficzne BSP, konwersji w locie do zgrupowanych warstw tymczasowych wraz ze stylizacją. Pozwala na: 1. Pobieranie struktur z podziałem hierarchicznym i zaawansowanym grupowaniem.
2.Selektywne filtrowanie wysokości do zadanego progu w metrach AGL.
3. Ograniczanie zasięgu na podstawie warstwy buforowej/maski lotów.
4. Dynamiczne etykietowanie stref i definiowanie kontrastowych podświetleń.
Wtyczka do poprawnego działania wymaga zestawu standardowych bibliotek. W środowiskach Windows i OS X instalatory QGIS dostarczają je domyślnie. W niektórych dystrybucjach Linux konieczna może być ich manualna weryfikacja. Przed uruchomieniem wtyczki upewnij się, że w środowisku interpreterów Pythona QGIS zainstalowane są pakiety: requests i urllib3
[EN]
The plugin allows for direct download of KML files representing airspace structures and UAS geographical zones directly from the official PANSA server interface (api.dronemap.pansa.pl), with on-the-fly conversion into styled, grouped memory layers. It features: 1. Downloading structures with hierarchical division and advanced grouping.
2. Selective altitude filtering up to a specified threshold in meters AGL.
3. Restricting the extent based on a buffer layer or a flight mask.
4. Dynamic zone labeling and defining high-contrast highlights.
The plugin requires a set of standard libraries to function properly. In Windows and OS X environments, QGIS installers provide them by default. In some Linux distributions, manual verification may be necessary. Before running the plugin, make sure that the 'requests' and 'urllib3' packages are installed in the QGIS Python interpreter environment.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Marcin Kelm (KELM Solutions) supported by Gemini and Claude AI

pyqgis_plugin.name: Thermal Temperature Reconstructor
pyqgis_plugin.description:
EN: Thermal Temperature Reconstructor is a QGIS plugin that recovers temperature values from thermal orthomosaics generated via DJI FlightHub 2 cloud mapping, which lose radiometric data during processing. Using a reverse calculation based on the color palette and the min/max temperature scale set during the flight mission, it rebuilds a raster containing actual temperature values. Tested with the Rainbow ISO 2 palette on DJI Matrice 4TD and Matrice 400 (H30T) imagery.
IT: Thermal Temperature Reconstructor è un plugin QGIS che recupera i valori di temperatura dagli ortomosaici termici generati con il cloud mapping di DJI FlightHub 2, che perdono i dati radiometrici durante l'elaborazione. Tramite un calcolo a ritroso basato sulla palette colori e sulla scala di temperatura min/max impostata durante la missione di volo, ricostruisce un raster contenente i valori reali di temperatura. Testato con la palette Rainbow ISO 2 su immagini DJI Matrice 4TD e Matrice 400 (H30T).
pyqgis_plugin.about:
EN: The Thermal Temperature Reconstructor plugin allows the reconstruction of temperature values from maps created with DJI drones, such as the Matrice 4TD and Matrice 400 with H30T, processed in the cloud on the DJI FlightHub 2 platform (cloud mapping), generating a map containing the temperature values. Cloud mapping reconstructions, in fact, lose the radiometric temperature information.
The process is based on a reverse calculation of the color palette and of the maximum and minimum temperature values set in the temperature scale during the flight mission.
The color palette we tested the workflow with is Rainbow ISO 2; under normal conditions, the ideal temperature scale is 0 to 130 °C. The temperature scale must be adjusted for each mission to prevent the cloud from failing to correctly reconstruct the thermal map: since the output is an orthophoto, it is essential that the thermal images are as little monochromatic as possible. Do not leave the temperature scale in dynamic mode, otherwise you will never obtain correct data!
IT: Il plugin Thermal Temperature Reconstructor permette di ricostruire i valori di temperatura delle cartografie realizzate con droni DJI, come Matrice 4TD e Matrice 400 con H30T, elaborate in cloud sulla piattaforma DJI FlightHub 2 (cloud mapping), generando una mappa contenente i valori di temperatura. Le ricostruzioni in cloud mapping, infatti, perdono l'informazione radiometrica di temperatura.
Il processo si basa su un calcolo a ritroso della scala colori e dei valori di temperatura massima e minima impostati nella scala di temperatura durante la missione di volo.
La scala colori con cui abbiamo testato il flusso di lavoro è la Rainbow ISO 2; in condizioni normali, la scala di temperatura ideale è da 0 a 130 °C. La scala di temperatura deve essere adattata a ogni missione, per evitare che il cloud non riesca a ricostruire correttamente la mappa termica: trattandosi di un'ortofoto, è fondamentale che le foto termiche siano il meno monocromatiche possibile. Non lasciare la scala di temperatura in modalità dinamica, altrimenti non otterrai mai dati corretti!

pyqgis_plugin.name: ArchaeoAstroInsight
pyqgis_plugin.description: Detects archaeological features in satellite and aerial imagery and computes their archaeoastronomical alignment by using AI algorithms.
pyqgis_plugin.about: ArchaeoAstroInsight is a QGIS plugin for the archaeoastronomical analysis of ground-level archaeological features. It detects features in satellite or aerial rasters using a YOLO model, estimates each feature's orientation (azimuth) with a ResNet classifier, derives the local horizon from either the HeyWhatsThat online service or user-provided SRTM elevation data, and computes the astronomical declination of each alignment. It also generates azimuth and declination curvigrams (kernel-density plots with significance thresholds) and writes all results to a single CSV for further analysis. It requires external Python packages (PyTorch, TensorFlow, Ultralytics and others) that are not bundled with the plugin; see the installation instructions in the repository README.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Andrei Ancuta, Helga Hochbauer, Maitane Urrutia, Marc Frincu

pyqgis_plugin.name: Flood Simulation Studio
pyqgis_plugin.description: Interactive flood simulation and return-period flood assessment tools for QGIS 3.x and 4.x.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Flood Simulation Studio is a standalone QGIS workspace for planning-grade flood simulation and return-period screening. Load an AOI, optional buildings, optional soil/drainage/surface-water layers, or let the Studio fetch DEM, SoilGrids soil parameters, and mapped surface water. Set rainfall, infiltration, drainage, channels, blockages, and timing, then run an animated 2D/3D flood scenario or T5-T100 return-period assessments. Outputs include maximum and final flood depth, flood extent, hazard, speed and direction proxies, water-surface raster, affected-structure counts, CSV summaries, scenario JSON, and transferable DEM/soil/surface-water context layers. Engineering certification should use calibrated local hydrology and approved hydraulic solvers.

Divide automaticamente áreas de APP em 5 partes iguais e áreas de Reserva Legal em 10 partes iguais, utilizando algoritmo otimizado de divisão por faixas com busca binária.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Observearth
pyqgis_plugin.description: Discover, visualize, and analyze satellite imagery with advanced spectral indices directly in QGIS.
pyqgis_plugin.about:
Observearth is a powerful QGIS plugin developed by the makers of Observearth (https://observearth.com) for discovering, visualizing, and analyzing satellite imagery directly within QGIS. The plugin integrates seamlessly with STAC (SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog) services, allowing users to search, preview, and process Earth observation imagery without leaving their GIS workflow.
Designed for GIS professionals, researchers, agronomists, environmental analysts, and remote sensing specialists, Observearth simplifies satellite data analysis with a fast, intuitive, and efficient interface.
Key Features: • Search satellite imagery using STAC catalogs. • Filter imagery by date range, cloud cover, satellite mission, and area of interest. • Generate and visualize spectral indices such as NDVI, EVI, and many more. • Display imagery directly within QGIS. • Automatic raster rendering with optimized visualization. • View raster statistics including minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation. • Fast loading and efficient processing for large datasets. • Cloud-optimized workflows with seamless Observearth integration.
Whether you're monitoring crop health, assessing vegetation, tracking environmental changes, or analyzing land cover, Observearth provides a streamlined workflow for accessing and analyzing satellite imagery—all from within QGIS.

Adds quick "flash" actions in three places:
Plugin toolbar (two buttons): • Flash selected features — flashes selected features on the active layer (red) • Flash selected vs rest — flashes selected features red and all other visible features blue simultaneously
Layers panel context menu (right-click a vector layer): • Flash selected features • Flash selected vs rest
Attribute table: • Toolbar buttons — same two actions as above, acting on the table's own layer • Row right-click — "Flash this feature" flashes the individual row you right-clicked • Hover — moving the mouse over a row flashes that feature (debounced, 120 ms)
Compatible with QGIS 3 (Qt5/PyQt5) and QGIS 4 (Qt6/PyQt6) via runtime detection. No external dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: TECRS Building Height Extractor
pyqgis_plugin.description: Extracts building heights from VHR satellite imagery shadows using vertex-comb ray casting.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The TECRS Building Height Extractor is a geospatial processing tool designed to estimate building heights from Very High-Resolution (VHR) satellite imagery. By inputting 2D building footprints, shadow polygons, and the image capture time, the plugin automatically computes the solar azimuth and elevation angles. It utilizes a Vertex Comb ray-casting algorithm to accurately associate buildings with their cast shadows, calculates the maximum shadow length, and computes the building height in meters using ellipsoidal trigonometry. This tool is ideal for urban planning and remote sensing workflows where 3D extraction from 2D optical imagery is required.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Layer or Table Comparison Tool
pyqgis_plugin.description: Compares vector layers and tables to find differences between selected fields
pyqgis_plugin.about: Professional tool for comparing vector layers and tables based on an alphanumeric field (codes, IDs, names, etc.). Offers three comparison modes: Only in Layer 1 (values present solely in the first layer), Only in Layer 2 (values present solely in the second layer), and Matches (identifies values existing in both layers but with different record counts). Generates detailed statistics such as total records per layer, unique values per layer, exact matches, quantity differences, and exclusive elements from each layer. Automatically creates a temporary table with the analysis results. Includes a progress bar for visual tracking, a log panel with real-time process details, and a user-friendly interface with color-coded buttons. Ideal for validation and quality control of geographic data, data migration, source integration, inventory auditing, and detection of missing or surplus records.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Cxf_in
pyqgis_plugin.description: Caricatore file CXF Catasto
pyqgis_plugin.about: GEOREFERENZIAZIONE FILE CATASTALI CXF DI TUTTA L'ITALIA La necessità di registrarsi per la georeferenziazione serve a garantire la qualità del dato e a non far proliferare sistemi di georeferenziazione che farebbero confusione. La procedura di georiferimento attuale è univoca (trasformazione di datum) e riguarda in maniera omogenea tutti i fogli dell'intero del Comune di riferimento. Per migliorare la georeferenziazione all'interno del singolo Comune deve essere applicata una trasformazione per singoli fogli. La procedure di georiferimento dei singoli fogli è presente per la Regione Friuli Venezia Giulia. Attendo progetti specifici per ampliare la gereferenziazione per singolo foglio per altre parti del territorio italiano. Cxf_in carica la trasformazione globale (trasformazione di datum) e se la trova successivamente applica i parametri di correzione al singolo foglio L'applicativo per la trasformazione è già pronto. Tale procedura necessita dei fogli catastali vettorilai. Per avere informazioni non esitate a scrivermi. Per informazioni scrivere a saccon@gisplan.it

Beknopt overzicht van functionaliteiten: - Zoeken op adres (gewoon, in batch en prikken op kaart) op basis van Gebouwen- en Adressenregister Vlaanderen. - Zoeken naar interessante plaatsen (POI) in Geopunt - Hoogteprofielen genereren - Zoeken naar percelen - Zoeken naar kaartlagen via Datavindplaats EN: Geopunt4QGIS – “Geopunt for QGIS” is the plug-in for the QGIS open-source desktop GIS that exposes the web services of Digitaal Vlaanderen and other agencies of the Flemish government to desktop GIS users. Digitaal Vlaanderen provides a range of geographic services (web services) that may be used by third parties, such as other public authorities and companies. Brief overview of functionalities: - Geocoding (standard, batch, and reverse), based on the Buildings and Address Registry Flanders. - Search for points of interest (POI) in Geopunt. - Generate elevation profiles. - Search for parcels. - Search for layers via the Datavindplaats.

It uses the local Geoid (GEOVALLE 1.0) (Opensource) developed by the regional autonomous corporation (CVC). For more information about the geoidal model GEOVALLE 1.0 please refer to http://www.cvc.gov.co/

pyqgis_plugin.name: topog4qgis

pyqgis_plugin.description: Export several print layouts to pdf, svg or image file (jpg, tif, png...) format in one click, from the current project or from projects in a folder.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Exporting a print layout requires to open it, launch the export, wait till it finishes. This procedure can become boring, repulsive and time consuming when you have to export a lot of print layouts. Maps Printer offers a quick way to export print layouts, without opening each one before: just check them in a list and launch their export to the file format you wish (pdf, svg, jpg, tif, png...). Furthermore, you can export print layouts from project files within a directory.
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Harrissou Sant-anna (Conseil d'Architecture, d'Urbanisme et de l'Environnement du Maine-et-Loire)

pyqgis_plugin.name: QuickOSM

pyqgis_plugin.about: Execute customs Overpass queries in QGIS to get OSM data.

pyqgis_plugin.name: norGIS ALKIS-Einbindung
pyqgis_plugin.description: This plugin is dealing with German cadastre data (therefore not localized)
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS-Erweiterung zur ALKIS-Einbindung Funktion: * Einbinden von durch norGIS ALKIS-Import vorbereitete Datenbanken. * Einbinden in QGIS * Export von UMN-Mapfiles (optional, erfordert python-mapscript) * Signaturierung nach GeoInfoDok * Eigentümerabfrage (Einzelabfragen) * Client für norGIS Liegenschaftsbuch

pyqgis_plugin.name: Dissolve with stats
pyqgis_plugin.description: Group entities with same value for one field, calculate statistics on the other fields
pyqgis_plugin.about: Choose a layer and a field for this layer. This plugin will merge all entities with the same value for this field, and can calculate statistics for each remaining field : min, max, sum, count, mean, median, standard deviation, first, last, concatenation and uniquification. Uniquification concatenate all values from a field without any duplicate. For example, from a polygon layer of provinces, with a country ID field and a population field, you can create a country layer with the sum of the population of its provinces for each country.

pyqgis_plugin.name: OpenQuake Integrated Risk Modelling Toolkit
pyqgis_plugin.description: Tools to drive the OpenQuake Engine, running calculations and visualizing their parameters and outputs
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin allows users to drive OpenQuake Engine calculations (https://github.com/gem/oq-engine) of physical hazard and risk, and to load the corresponding outputs as QGIS layers. For those outputs, data visualization tools are provided.

pyqgis_plugin.name: NNJoin
pyqgis_plugin.description: Nearest neighbour join. Join vector layers based on nearest neighbour relationships.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The NNPlugin joins two vector layers (the input and the join layer) based on nearest neighbour relationships. All geometry type combinations are supported. A feature from the input layer is joined to the nearest feature in the join layer. The result of the join is a new vector layer with the same geometry type and coordinate reference system as the input layer. Joining layers with different Coordinate Reference Systems (CRS) is supported, as long as the join layer coordinate system is a projected CRS. The join and distance calculations is performed using the join layer CRS. Self joins are supported. For self joins, each feature in the layer is joined to its nearest neighbour within the layer. A spatial index (QgsSpatialIndex) on the join layer is used to speed up the join for layers with non-multi-geometry types.

pyqgis_plugin.name: VectorMCDA
pyqgis_plugin.description: Performs geographic multi-criteria decision making. Plugin is now deprecated, the MCDA functions are all implemented and extended in SSAM plugin
pyqgis_plugin.about: VectorMCDA is a QGIS plugin that uses different MCDA algorithms to perform a multicriteria analysis in a geographic environmental

pyqgis_plugin.name: Mutant
pyqgis_plugin.description: Display values from loaded raster layers in a table or plot optionally ordered by time which can be extracted from the layername (or other sources).
pyqgis_plugin.about: Display raster layer values at current mouse position ordered by time. Time can be extracted on the fly from Layer(File)name or other sources. Used Layers can easily be selected by using expressions.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Multi-distance buffer
pyqgis_plugin.description: Create multiple distance buffers
pyqgis_plugin.about: The Multi-Distance Buffer plugin creates a multi-distance buffer vector layer from an input vector layer and a set of distances. The result layer consists of bands (donut type) of regions according to the buffer distances provided. If 100 and 200 are provided as distances, the result layer will consist of two bands - one will contain all areas that are within 100 units from the geometries of the input vector layer, the other will contain all areas that are from 100 to 200 units from the geometries of the input vector layer. The user can choose to only buffer around selected features. Negative buffer distances are allowed for polygon layers.

pyqgis_plugin.name: STEM
pyqgis_plugin.description: Sistema di TElerilevamento e di Monitoraggio del territorio e dell'ambiente trentino
pyqgis_plugin.about: Plugin to analize hyperspectral and lidar data for Provincia Autonoma di Trento, Italian language is used for plugin interface
pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Angelo Carriero, Michele Fioretto, Fabio Roncato, Thomas Maffei, Stefano Piffer, Michele Dalponte

pyqgis_plugin.name: Spreadsheet Layers
pyqgis_plugin.description: Load layers from spreadsheet files (*.ods, *.xls, *.xlsx)
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin adds a "Add spreadsheet layer" entry in "Layer" / "Add new Layer" menu and a corresponding button in the "Layers" toolbar. These two links open the same dialog to load a layer from a spreadsheet file (*.ods, *.xls, *.xlsx) with some options (use header at first line, ignore some rows and optionally load geometry from x and y fields). When this dialog is accepted, it creates a new GDAL VRT file in same folder as the source data file and layer name, expanded with a .vrt suffix which is loaded into QGIS using OGR VRT driver. When reusing the same file twice, the dialog loads its values from the existing .vrt file. No need to install additional dependencies.

pyqgis_plugin.name: CLUZ4

pyqgis_plugin.about: The CLUZ (Conservation Land-Use Zoning) plugin lets people design conservation area and nature recovery networks through on-screen conservation planning. It also acts as an interface for the Marxan and Marxan with Zones software package.
pyqgis_plugin.tags: marxan,spatial conservation prioritisation,systematic conservation planning,gap analysis

pyqgis_plugin.name: Bulk vector export as SLD and GeoJson
pyqgis_plugin.description: Export all vector layers as GeoJSON and SLD.
pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin exports all vector layers as GeoJSON with their SLD styling. Active raster layers are exported according to their position in the layer stack as multiband GeoTIFFs. The resulting files are zipped into a file named after the QGIS project. The layer order and additional information is stored in a metadata.json. Basemap PNG tiles are ignored at export.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Complex GML Info

pyqgis_plugin.author_name: Juergen Weichand, Tim Vinzing, Edward Nash, Wilhelm Beiche

pyqgis_plugin.about: Literature Mapper inserts geoJSON geometry strings into an online Zotero database to facilitate the mapping of study site locations. The locations stored in the database are displayed on the map canvas in virtual point and multipoint shapefiles on start up.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Place Marker
pyqgis_plugin.description: Place Marker provides a convenient way of adding placemarks to a vector layer.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Place Marker provides a quick and easy way of creating point layers and adding features with preset attributes. Unlike using the built-in editing tools, the created layer contains the necessary attributes, and newly added features are committed directly to the data store and should be available immediately on other QGIS instances. It addresses to usage scenarios where QGIS in conjunction with the "PosiView" plugin serves as an online visualization and navigation tool, e.g for scientific subsea surveys with remotely operated or autonomous vehicles. It allows marking and sharing interesting places and events during the dive.

pyqgis_plugin.about: GeODin is an industry standard software for the collection, interpretation and presentation of geo-information. GeODinQGIS is an additional tool for the work with GeODin. It connects GeODin with QGIS.

pyqgis_plugin.about: This plugin facilitates access to geographic data. It is a geographic metadata search engine based on the <a href="https://www.isogeo.com/">Isogeo</a> API.

pyqgis_plugin.about: Search for published collections and install them for use with QGIS. Symbology (SVG, images, styles), Processing scripts, Processing models, R scripts and checklists are supported. There are several options for repositories: Github, Bitbucket, local file system and HTTP(S).

pyqgis_plugin.name: JoinSplit
pyqgis_plugin.description: JoinSplit relates a spatial layer with a matrix sharing a common field, and export the selected fields from the matrix as spatial layers.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The JoinSplit works by performing a table join between a spatial layer and a matrix (opened as a table in QGIS), and it exports each field from the matrix, or only those selected by the user, as an individual shapefile. This plugin is useful when a matrix of presence or counts of multiple entities (e.g. species observations) are available with an grid identifier (e.g. UTM square, custom grid ID, intersection of lat/lon with a grid, etc). The JoinSplit opens all layers in the Table of Contents and the user may choose a style file (exported from any other shapefile) to show the new layers. The plugin includes an example data set (more details in the homepage).

pyqgis_plugin.name: Table to Style
pyqgis_plugin.description: Reads an attribute table (usually in dbf or text format) with pixel value information and attributes and creates a new style for raster display.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The Table2Style links an attribute table with pixel value colour information with a pixel value of a raster, displaying the raster as intended. The colour information is the red, green and blue values (from 0 to 1 or 0 to 255) and, optionally, the opacity. The plugin also creates a random color scheme for each pixel value, if no file is available. A simple example data set is provided.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Hotspot Analysis

Input data must be a shapefile of points or polygons with an associated projected coordinate system and (at least) one numeric attribute. The plugin requires PySAL 2 (see the repository for installation instruction).

Satellite Brightness Temperature > Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) > Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) > True Color Composite (TCC) > Flase Color Composite (FCC) > At Satellite Reflectance of available bands > At Satellite Radiance of available bands > Other user defined custom band outputs

pyqgis_plugin.name: Select by relationship
pyqgis_plugin.description: The plugin allows to select records through tables based on relationships one-to-one or one-to-many specified inside a QGIS project.
pyqgis_plugin.about: The plugin allows to select records through tables based on relationships one-to-one or one-to-many specified inside a QGIS project.<br>The plugin button will appear inside QGIS database menu. Anything in 3 steps:<br>1.Charge in a QGIS project your layers;<br>2.Set up the relationships between your layers inside the QGIS project properties;<br>3.Click on selectFromRelations button (or run its from QGIS toolbar Database->Select From Relation -> Allow selections by relationship.<br><br>Now you can select records between many related tables.<br>You can see an example in this videotutorial by Salvatore Fiandaca: <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4lXRnsMO-qI">link</a><br>The plugin started by an original thread posted by Salvatore Fiandaca and developed by Andrea Borruso and Salvatore Larosa: <a href="http://osgeo-org.1560.x6.nabble.com/QGIS-select-in-join-tabella-in-relazione-td5317093.html">Original thread</a><br>A first post by Andrea Borruso: <a href="https://medium.com/tantotanto/qgis-selezionare-geometrie-da-una-tabella-di-attributi-correlata-bea37747a7e2">link</a><br>The original python macro by Salvatore Larosa: <a href="https://gist.github.com/slarosa/653e6d759cf0d82c2a24dcc499b094e0">link</a><br>A videotutorial by Salvatore Fiandaca where it's showed the use of python macro by Salvatore Larosa: <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRDftcPWNg8">link</a><br>An other videotutorial by Salvatore Fiandaca for testing the macro python code embedded inside selectFromRelations plugin: <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4lXRnsMO-qI">link</a>

pyqgis_plugin.name: Vector Tiles Reader
pyqgis_plugin.description: Reader (short VT reader) which reads Vector Tiles from various predefined and configurable sources
pyqgis_plugin.about: Plugin which reads vector tiles according to Mapbox' Vector Tiles specification as QGIS layers in a group. Styled vector tiles are typically used as high quality base maps. Sources can be an internet server, an MBTiles file or a directory of files. If an Mapbox GL JSON style is configured, the style is (partially) converted to QGIS styles. The plugin has connections already configured for the following providers: * MapTiler.com * Nextzen.org * OpenInfraMap.org This Python plugin uses prebuilt C++ binaries for performance reasons.

pyqgis_plugin.about: this plugin pile up the polygons of a layer and copy them in a new layer in a pyramid-like way, that is to say with the smallests on top of the largest's ones, in order to let the users see as many objects as possible when opening the layer without using the style properties.
pyqgis_plugin.tags: tools,polygons orderer by size- python qgis

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoTrace
pyqgis_plugin.description: Collection of tools extracting trace data from commonly used geoscience rasters such as imagery, topography and geophysics.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GeoTrace is a a QGIS plugin containing some helpful tools for extracting and analysing the orientations of geological structures. It can be used to rapidly digitize structural traces in raster data, estimate their 3D orientations using an associated DEM, and then visualise the results on stereonets and rose diagrams. There is a complementary plugin, Compass, for CloudCompare that provides similar functionalities for 3D point clouds. The trace extraction method (Trace tab) uses a least-cost path algorithm to "follow" linear features in the raster. This relies on a single-channel cost raster in which the structures of interest are represented by low values, and the background by high values. A variety of functions for quickly calculating such a cost function have been included in the Cost Calculator tab. See the about tab for more information and a quick guide on how to use the plugin

pyqgis_plugin.name: ZoomToBelgium
pyqgis_plugin.description: A button to zoom to any of the Belgian administrative boundaries (country, region, community, province, municipality or district). Een knop om naar één van de Belgische administratieve grenzen te zoomen (land, gewest, gemeenschap, provincie, gemeente of district).
